# GPT Realtime Assistant

> GPT Realtime Assistant is a live AI assistant for iPhone, iPad and Mac. It translates a conversation between two people both ways and reads each translation aloud, writes a live transcript and answers questions as people talk.

GPT Realtime Assistant is a live AI assistant for iPhone, iPad and Mac. It
listens to the conversation you are in and helps while it is still going on:
it writes a live transcript, answers the question on the table as people talk,
and translates a conversation between two people both ways, reading each
translation aloud, or one way into the language you choose. Made by Arte Soft EOOD; not affiliated with OpenAI.

Devices: iPhone and iPad on iOS/iPadOS 26 or later, and Mac. One subscription
covers all three.

What it does:

- Live transcript with the assistant's answers beside it, in brief, balanced or
  detailed length; the assistant answers each turn by itself, and you can
  interrupt an answer by speaking
- Two-way translation ("Translate both ways"): choose two of 58 languages; each
  person speaks in turn in their own language, and every sentence appears in
  the other language, read aloud when "Speak translations" is on (on by
  default). It runs two translations at once, about 85 credits a minute, so
  the 2,000 monthly credits cover roughly 23 minutes of it (and the 48,000
  annual credits on the yearly plan cover roughly 564 minutes across the year)
- One-way translation: the spoken language is detected (or set) and each
  sentence appears in the language you choose moments after the speaker
  pauses, and can be read aloud
- Seventeen session templates with roles and instructions already written
  (interview, negotiation, sprint planning, daily standup, client discovery,
  sales demo, support triage, incident review, design review, user research,
  lecture notes, one-on-one, hiring debrief, decision meeting, translation,
  coding task, product review), or a blank session with your own instructions
- Photos and screenshots as context for the answers
- Projects, sessions, a task board (status, priority, dates, comments) and a
  scheduler with reminders; useful moments become tasks with one tap
- Karaoke readback: the text highlights word by word as you read it aloud,
  recognised on the device, for rehearsing a talk or practising a language
- Mac only: system audio (the other side of a video call), capture of a chosen
  screen or window as context, recording it with its sound as a video, and
  Notes
- Mac with Apple silicon only: Whisper Large v3 Turbo and Qwen 3 8B, downloaded
  once in Settings, then run on the Mac itself without the cloud and without
  spending credits (local answers are text only)

What it does not do: it does not transcribe recordings or audio files after
the fact, write summaries or minutes on its own, or export sessions. It works
live, while the session runs, with the app open on screen: a live session
ends if the app goes to the background or the phone locks. There is no free
trial.

What it costs: the app is free to download and needs an active subscription to
run: either 9.99 USD a month (with 2,000 AI credits each month) or 79.99 USD a
year (with 48,000 AI credits per annual payment — equivalent to 4,000 credits a
month, 2× the monthly credit rate while saving ~33% compared with twelve monthly
payments). Credit packs of 1,000 (4.99 USD) and 5,000 (19.99 USD) add more. A
thousand credits are one US dollar of model usage at OpenAI's list rates.
Credits are spent on the audio and text a cloud session uses; two-way
translation costs about 85 credits a minute; local sessions on a Mac use none.
Purchases go through Apple.

Privacy: during a cloud session, audio goes from the device directly to
OpenAI's Realtime API. Arte Soft's backend issues a short-lived session secret
and records usage and purchases; it never receives audio, transcripts or
answers. Sessions, transcripts, tasks and notes are stored on the device, with
no cloud sync.

This site publishes 100 English guides organized by task: voice conversations,
meeting records, transcription troubleshooting, interview and presentation
practice, language learning, translation, image context, projects and task
follow-up. The guides include worked examples, verification checklists and
links to supporting publisher documentation. Twenty-four of the guides, on
translation, transcripts, the assistant and costs, are also published in all
twenty-nine languages of the site.

Version: 1.2 on the App Store since 4 October 2026, on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
Two-way translation and spoken translations are part of it. iPhone and iPad
cloud sessions need an internet connection; offline use is the Mac's local
models only.
